# Brand assets

**Generated. Do not edit anything in this folder, and do not add to it.**

This is a `brandkit bundle` of the `daynnight` brand, written whole by the
brand kit from `brands/daynnight/brand.toml`. The kit is a separate, private
repository - it is the source of truth for these files and is not needed to
build or run this application. Everything here except this file came out of
**brandkit 1.55.0**, and `BUNDLE.json` beside it lists every file with its
hash.

Two commands, run from a checkout of the kit, with `$DAYANDNIGHT` set to a
checkout of this repository:

```
PYTHONPATH=src python -m brandkit bundle daynnight "$DAYANDNIGHT/app/brand"
PYTHONPATH=src python -m brandkit check  daynnight "$DAYANDNIGHT/app/brand"
```

`check` is the one that matters: it says what is missing, what somebody edited
in place, and what is in here that the brand never contained. It compares
against the brand *as it is now*, so once the brand moves on it reports the
difference rather than a pass - which is the point of it, and which is how the
1.55.0 rebuild was noticed three days after it happened. An edit here is lost
at the next `bundle`; an edit in the brand definition is the one that lasts.

`BRAND.md` in this folder is the kit's own documentation, generated by the same
build that wrote the files, and is the only thing that can be trusted to name
them correctly. Read it before using anything here.

## What this application uses

The bundle is a complete set for an application, a website and a repository,
and this product is only one of those - so most of it is unused, and that is
fine. The folder shape is load-bearing: every stylesheet in `template/` reaches
its neighbours as `../font/`, `../mark/` and `../wordmark/`, so nothing may be
flattened or moved.

| Path                          | Where it is used                                       |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `mark/mark.svg`               | the symbol, top left of the sidebar (`app/index.html`) |
| `wordmark/wordmark-light.svg` | the name beside it, on a light background              |
| `wordmark/wordmark-dark.svg`  | the name beside it, on a dark background               |
| `template/fonts.css`          | declares both faces; imported by `app/styles.css`      |
| `template/tokens.css`         | `--font` and `--font-display`; imported under a layer  |
| `font/publicsans.woff`        | what the editor is read in, loaded by `fonts.css`      |
| `font/jost.woff`              | what the name and the headings are drawn in            |
| `icon/favicon.ico`            | the Windows application icon (`electron-builder.yml`)  |

The mark and the wordmark are shipped SVGs rather than type set in CSS, and the
family is named by the kit's own token sheet rather than by ours, so the
application and the brand cannot drift apart. `app/styles.css` explains why the
kit's tokens are imported into a CSS layer underneath this project's own.

`template/base.css`, `components.css` and `layout.css` are a UI shell this
application does not use - it has `app/styles.css` - and `social/`, `web/` and
`theme/` are for a website it does not have. They stay because the bundle is
the unit `check` verifies; picking files out of it is how two applications
built from one brand end up with two layouts and no way to compare them.

## When the brand changes

Re-run `bundle`, then `check`, then look at three things:

1. **The typefaces.** They are third-party licences in a proprietary product.
   `licenses/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` names them and `licenses/third-party/`
   carries their texts; `desktop/build/check-bundle.js` fails the build if one
   is missing. A face added, dropped or swapped means all three change - which
   is what happened at 1.55.0, when the brand gained a second face to be read
   in and Jost moved to headings only.
2. **The icon.** `electron-builder.yml` points `win.icon` straight at
   `icon/favicon.ico` in here, so a new icon needs no copying - but a bundle
   that stops shipping that file breaks the build, which is the point.
3. **The paths.** `app/index.html` and `app/styles.css` name files in here by
   their folder. A browser test asserts the mark and both wordmarks actually
   load, and another asserts the face does, so a renamed file fails a test
   rather than silently showing nothing.

## The name

The product is **Day and Night** in every sentence - this file, the EULA, the
installer, the window title. **DAYnNIGHT** is how the name is drawn, and it
only appears as the wordmark. `licenses/TRADEMARKS.md` claims both.
